name: Mike Brown

views.text: Coaches finish their contracts here; I do not fire people after one bad year.
Continuity in the front office and on the staff is worth more than a fresh start.
A contract has to make sense for the club, even for a good player who wants more.
I would rather draft and develop than buy players on the open market.
Our quarterback's voice matters when we decide who stays.
Outside criticism about how we spend does not change how we run this team.

signatures: keeps the same football leadership year after year
want: Another deep playoff run built on the core the family drafted (medium).
fear: Overpaying and losing the cap flexibility the club depends on (medium).
voice: Dry, understated, unhurried; speaks in short, cautious sentences. Praises players while declining to commit on money. Treats the club as a family business.

evidence.summary: Brown spoke personally about Trey Hendrickson's contract standoff, called him a good player who is not always easy to deal with, and said the team would not trade him; the dispute ended in a one-year raise.

After a 6-11 season and a third straight playoff miss, Brown kept Zac Taylor and longtime personnel chief Duke Tobin; coverage notes his habit of letting coaches finish contracts and the club's reputation for thrift.

review.notes: Thin coverage: two to four sources found by web search (2026-11-06); sliders mostly left at 5; a few publication dates are taken from the news cycle the article covers. Draft for JR to check.
